findings.summary: crates/server/src/board.rs:66 pr_for: no test covers a ticket with two PRs on branches that name it. With the key changed to (by_branch, Reverse(number)), which shows the oldest, every test still passes. The e2e run with the made-up #903 and #49 showed the newest, as built.

crates/server/src/github.rs:60: no test covers a branch and a title that name different tickets. Swapping the order to title first, then branch, still passes every test. The e2e run showed the branch winning (#902, titled 'TRU-6: misc' on fix/tru-7-thing, went to TRU-7).

crates/server/src/github.rs:96 still reads only check-runs. A PR with no check runs, or with only commit statuses, stays 'pending' and never reaches Needs you. Carried over from rounds 1 and 2; seen in the code here, not reproduced with real data.

crates/server/src/main.rs:16 the GitHub source refreshes every 60s. One read for the two configured repos made 8 GitHub requests with only 2 tied PRs, which is about 480 an hour, well past the 60-an-hour unauthenticated limit that main.rs's own comment mentions.
